'''Baldev Singh Dhillon''' (born 27 June 1947) is an Indian agricultural scientist. He is known for his contributions to [[plant breeding]], [[genetics]], and [[plant genetic resources]], particularly in [[maize]] [[Plant breeding|breeding]]. Currently, he is vice president of [[National Academy of Agricultural Sciences]] since January 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ex-PAU VC Dr Baldev Singh Dhillon appointed NAAS vice-president for 3-year term |url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/ex-pau-vc-dr-baldev-singh-dhillon-appointed-naas-vice-president-for-3-year-term/ |access-date=2025-06-10 |website=The Tribune |language=en}}</ref> Previously he served as vice-chancellor of the [[Punjab Agricultural University]] from July 2011 to June 2021, leading the institution to notable recognition, including being ranked 2nd by the [[Indian Council of Agricultural Research]] (ICAR) in 2017.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-06-30 |title=Baldev Singh Dhillon to continue as Punjab Agricultural University vice-chancellor |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/ludhiana/bs-dhillon-to-continue-as-pau-vc/articleshow/83964061.cms |access-date=2025-06-10 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=8 December 2021 |title=ICAR rankings: PAU slips to second spot among country’s agricultural universities |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/cities/chandigarh-news/icarrankingspau-slips-to-second-spot-among-country-s-agricultural-universities-101638905894248.html |access-date=10 June 2025 |work=Hindustan Times}}</ref>

Dhillon has held multiple roles such as assistant director general at the Indian Council of Agricultural Research, director of the National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources, and director of research at Punjab Agricultural University and [[Guru Nanak Dev University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=PunjabNewsline.com - Renowned Punjab maize breeder invited to join as Director Research in GNDU<!-- Bot generated title --> |url=http://www.punjabnewsline.com/content/view/4710/38/ |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071025070259/http://www.punjabnewsline.com/content/view/4710/38/ |archivedate=25 October 2007}}</ref> His international experience includes research positions at the [[University of Hohenheim]], Germany, the [[International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center]], Mexico, and the [[University of Birmingham]], UK.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baldev Singh Dhillon – BISA {{!}} Borlaug Institute for South Asia |url=https://bisa.org/about/governance/baldev-singh-dhillon/ |access-date=2025-06-10 |language=en-US}}</ref> Dhillon is fellow of [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] and [[Indian National Science Academy]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dhillon, Baldev Singh – The National Academy of Sciences, India |url=https://nasi.org.in/fellows/dhillon-baldev-singh/ |access-date=2025-06-10 |website=nasi.org.in}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=INSA :: Fellow Detail - Dr Baldev Singh Dhillon |url=https://insajournal.in/intranetinsa/fellow_detail.php?id=P00-1274 |access-date=2025-06-10 |website=insajournal.in}}</ref> Dhillon was honoured with the [[Padma Shri]] in 2019, Dhillon has published over 350 research papers and received multiple awards, including the [[Om Prakash Bhasin Award]] and the Dr. NL Dhawan Lifetime Achievement Award, for his contributions to agricultural science.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-07-10 |title=PAU bids adieu to its longest-serving vice chancellor, Padma Shri Dr BS Dhillon given warm farewell |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/ludhiana/pau-bids-adieu-to-its-longest-serving-vice-chancellor-padma-shri-dr-bs-dhillon-given-warm-farewell-7397889/ |access-date=2025-06-10 |website=The Indian Express |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Dhillon was born in [[Amritsar]] in 1947.<ref name="Indian National Science Academy" /> He is known for scientific breakthroughs in plant breeding.

{{More citations needed|date=March 2026}}


Dhillon did his B.Sc. in agriculture from Khalsa College, Amritsar; Post graduation M.Sc. from [[Punjab Agricultural University]] and Doctorate from the Indian Agricultural Research Institute ([[IARI]]), New Delhi. He has published 350 research publications and many books.
